title: Suraqah on the Road • Waiting at the Harrah • At Quba • Suhayb’s Gold • Where the She-Camel Knelt • From the Day the Years Were Counted • The First Word • Our Home Today • Final Word

blocks.1: After three nights they set out on the road. By then Quraysh had already announced. For the Prophet {{1}} and for Abu Bakr (RA), for each a reward equal to the blood-money of one man; for whoever would kill or capture them. A greedy hunter followed, lured by that reward. Suraqah ibn Malik.{{2}}
blocks.2: Abu Bakr (RA) has also told of that moment.
blocks.4: We set out, and the people were searching for us. No one caught up with us except Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, on his horse. I said, O Messenger of Allah, the pursuer has caught up with us. He said, do not grieve, Allah is with us.{{1}}
blocks.5: What happened, in his own words.
blocks.7: I could hear the recitation of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}; he did not look back, while Abu Bakr (RA) kept looking back. Then the front legs of my horse sank into the ground, up to the knees. I fell from the horse. I scolded it; it stood up, but could hardly get its legs out. When it stood upright, from the marks of its legs a column of dust, like smoke, rose into the sky.{{2}}
blocks.8: The horse was running toward the hunter; and the ground itself seized it. Suraqah threw the arrow-lots to see good and ill omen. The result he did not want came out. He threw again. Again the same. Then he called out asking for security. They stopped.
blocks.10: Then this belief arose in my heart: after the obstruction I met in reaching them, the matter of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} will surely prevail. I said to him, your people have announced a blood-money reward for you; and I told them the news of what people wanted to do with them. I offered them provisions and goods; they did not reduce anything of mine, nor asked anything of me, only said, keep our matter secret.{{2}}
blocks.11: He who came for the greed of a reward went away with a written paper of security in his hand.
blocks.13: One thing needs to be said from here. Most of the scenes in this part are at the end of hadith number 3906 of Sahih al-Bukhari. That part is the narration of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. He is a Tabi‘i; he told the events without naming any Companion. So that part is mursal. The main structure, however, is also in the sound narration of Anas (RA); the Ansar’s welcome at the Harrah, going around him bearing arms. The rest of the details have been taken as scenes.{{1}}
blocks.14: A caravan beside the road. A group of Muslim traders returning from Syria. Among them al-Zubayr (RA).
blocks.16: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} met al-Zubayr (RA) in a Muslim caravan, who were returning from trade in Syria. Al-Zubayr (RA) clothed the Messenger of Allah {{2}} and Abu Bakr (RA) in white garments.{{3}}
blocks.17: And one small matter of that road Anas (RA) has told. It is sound, from the mouth of a Companion.
blocks.19: The Prophet {{1}} was coming toward Madinah, with Abu Bakr (RA) riding behind him. Abu Bakr (RA) was elderly, a well-known face; and the Prophet {{2}} was young, unknown to people. Someone would meet Abu Bakr (RA) and say, O Abu Bakr, who is this man in front of you? He would say, this man guides me on the way. The listener would think he meant the road. In fact he meant the path of good.{{3}}
blocks.20: Not a lie. Not a hiding of a lie either. A word that is true, and at the same time leads the listener in another direction. Meanwhile in Madinah.
blocks.22: The Muslims in Madinah heard of the Messenger of Allah’s {{1}} leaving Makkah. Every morning they would go to the Harrah and wait for him, until the heat of noon sent them back. One day, after a long wait, they went back. When they had entered their houses, a Jew climbed up a high fortress of theirs for some purpose. He saw the Messenger of Allah {{2}} and his companions in white garments, the mirage moving away before them. He could not hold himself, and cried out at the top of his voice, O people of the Arabs, here is your good fortune that you were waiting for!{{3}}
blocks.23: Then what the Ansar did, in the words of Anas (RA),
blocks.25: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} alighted beside the Harrah, then sent for the Ansar. They came and greeted the two of them and said, mount, safe and obeyed. Then the Prophet {{2}} and Abu Bakr (RA) mounted, and the Ansar went around them with weapons in hand. In Madinah it was said, the Prophet of Allah has come, the Prophet of Allah has come!{{3}}
blocks.26: What they had promised on the night of ‘Aqabah, here they kept with their own hands.
blocks.28: Monday. The month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal. The Prophet {{1}} alighted in the upper part of the city, in the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf; that is Quba.{{2}}
blocks.31: Abu Bakr (RA) stood before the people, and the Messenger of Allah {{1}} sat silent. The Ansar who had not seen the Messenger of Allah {{2}} before came and began greeting Abu Bakr (RA). At last the sun fell on the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then Abu Bakr (RA) came forward and shaded him with his cloak. Only then did the people recognise the Messenger of Allah {{4}}.{{5}}
blocks.32: At Quba the Prophet {{1}} stayed fourteen nights.{{2}}
blocks.33: In these very days that mosque was founded whose foundation is on taqwa; the Prophet {{1}} prayed in it.{{2}}
blocks.34: ‘Ali (RA) arrived at Quba. Staying three more nights in Makkah he had returned, one by one, the trusts people had left with the Prophet {{1}}.{{2}}
blocks.35: At Quba he stayed near the house of a Muslim widow. At night he would see someone come and knock on her door, she comes out, the man leaves something. Suspicion arose in ‘Ali’s (RA) mind. He asked, servant of Allah, who is this who comes to your door every night? You are a Muslim woman, you have no husband. The woman said, this is Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). He knows I have no one. When evening comes he breaks the idols of his tribe, brings the pieces to me. He says, use these as fuel. ‘Ali (RA) kept in mind this deed of Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). After Sahl’s death, in Iraq, he himself told that story.{{1}}
blocks.37: While at Quba, one more arrived; leaving his gold. Suhayb (RA) had wanted to set out. Some youths of Quraysh stopped him. What happened then was in his own words.
blocks.39: I had intended to go out with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, but some youths of Quraysh stopped me. That night I kept standing up again and again, I did not sit. They said, Allah has kept him busy with his stomach. Yet I was not sick. They got up and left. I went out; after I had gone a ‘barid’, some of them caught up with me to bring me back. I said, do you want me to give you several uqiyyah of gold, and you leave my way and keep the promise made to me? They agreed. I went back with them to Makkah. I said, dig under the threshold of the door, there are uqiyyahs of gold; and go to such-and-such woman and take two sets of clothes. Then I set out and reached the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, before his moving away from Quba. Seeing me he said three times, O Abu Yahya, profitable was this trade! I said, O Messenger of Allah, no one came to you before me; no one informed you except Jibril (AS).{{3}}
blocks.40: He had bought the way with gold. And the word with which the Prophet {{1}} welcomed him is ‘profit’. What we count as loss, the Prophet {{2}} often calls profit.
blocks.42: After fourteen nights the Prophet {{1}} sent for Banu Najjar. That day Anas (RA) saw with his own eyes.
blocks.44: The Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, and alighted in the upper part of the city in a settlement named Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. There he stayed fourteen nights. Then he sent for Banu Najjar. They came with swords hanging. It is as if I am still seeing it, the Prophet {{2}} on his mount, Abu Bakr (RA) behind him, and the men of Banu Najjar around him; in this way he came and halted in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub (RA).{{3}}
blocks.45: From Quba the Prophet {{1}} set out on Friday. In the valley of Banu Salim ibn ‘Awf the time of Jumu‘ah came. He prayed in the mosque there. That is the first Jumu‘ah in Madinah. Then tribe after tribe came to block the way. ‘Utban of Banu Salim and ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah, stay with us. We have numbers, equipment, protection. The Prophet {{2}} said, ‘leave the she-camel’s way, she is commanded.’ Banu Bayadah came and said the same. The same reply. On behalf of Banu Sa‘idah, Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA). The same reply. On behalf of Banu al-Harith, Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA), Kharijah, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA). The same reply. Banu ‘Adi ibn Najjar, the tribe of his maternal uncles, said, your maternal uncles are here. The same reply.{{3}}
blocks.46: Every tribe wanted him to stay in their house. The Prophet {{1}} named no one. Wherever the she-camel goes. Exactly where the she-camel knelt, that account is in the narration of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. That part too is mursal.
blocks.48: Then he mounted his mount, and the people walked with him. At last the she-camel knelt at the place of the Messenger’s mosque in Madinah, where that day some Muslims were praying. The place was a date-drying yard of two orphan boys named Suhayl and Sahl, who were in the care of As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA). When the she-camel knelt with him, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, God willing, this is the dwelling.{{2}}
blocks.50: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} called the two boys, wanting to bargain for the yard to build a mosque. They said, no, O Messenger of Allah, we give it to you as a gift.{{2}}
blocks.51: In the narration of Anas (RA), however, the mention of the land comes in the name of Banu Najjar.{{1}}
blocks.52: Then the mosque began to rise. The narration of Anas (RA),
blocks.54: He ordered the building of the mosque. Calling the men of Banu Najjar he said, O Banu Najjar, fix the price of this garden of yours. They said, no, by Allah, we ask its price from no one but Allah. In it were graves of the polytheists, some ruins and date palms. The Prophet {{1}} gave the order; the graves were dug up and removed, the ruins were levelled, the date palms were cut down. The cut trunks were placed in a row toward the mosque’s qiblah, and stones were set on both sides of the door. They recited rhythmic verses as they carried the stones, and the Prophet {{2}} was with them; he was saying, O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter; so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.{{3}}
blocks.55: He who once went from market to market saying, who will give me shelter, is now carrying stones with his own hands.
blocks.56: From the Day the Years Were Counted
blocks.57: From which day does the Muslim nation’s calendar begin? It could have begun from the day the Prophet {{1}} received revelation. It could have begun from the day he passed away. In the words of Sahl ibn Sa‘d (RA) the counting began from another day.{{2}}
blocks.59: They did not count (the years) from the day the Prophet {{1}} received prophethood, nor even from the day of his passing; they counted only from the day of his arrival in Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.61: What was the Prophet’s {{1}} first word on the soil of Madinah? ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) was in the crowd that day. He is a man of the lineage of Bani Isra’il.
blocks.63: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} came to Madinah, people rushed toward him; it was said, the Messenger of Allah {{2}} has come. I too went with the people to see him. When the face of the Messenger of Allah {{3}} became clear to me, I understood that this face is not the face of a liar.{{4}}
blocks.64: And what he said first of all,
blocks.66: The first thing he said was: O people, spread the salam, feed food, and pray when people are asleep; you will enter Paradise in peace.{{1}}
blocks.67: In the first sermon there is no talk of war, no talk of power.
blocks.69: This story returns to our home today at several places. The first place is that of trust and calculation. In the Hijrah, in each task of the Prophet {{1}} there was one person. A person to gather news at night. A person to graze goats. A person to show the road. A person to lie in the bed. Four months of feeding two camels. Both together. The student who without opening the book says, Allah is my trust; he is not speaking of trust, he is giving his laziness a beautiful name. And the businessman who calculates everything, and still cannot sleep at night from uncertainty, has put the calculation itself in the place of Allah. The Prophet {{2}} showed; first the hand moves, then trust. Trust is not the name of sitting with hands folded.
blocks.70: The second place is that of giving shelter. For ten years the Prophet {{1}} called, who will give me shelter? Today that call comes in another language. A plot of land for a mosque. A good teacher for a madrasah. The study expenses of an orphan. A corner to lay one’s head for a servant of the din. The Ansar responded. About them the Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.72: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred for the Ansar.{{1}}
blocks.73: To love and honour those who give shelter to the din is itself a sign of faith. The third place is the gold of Suhayb (RA). Such a time comes before us too. A road of haram income. A file of bribery. A usurious dealing, in which everything is in order, only Allah’s permission is missing.
blocks.74: The fourth place is that of telling openly. On the night of ‘Aqabah As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) said, know the risk first, then stretch out the hand. No one kept anyone in the dark. Today when we call others to the path of the din, we do not tell of the hardship. We make a marriage proposal and hide the risk. We call someone to a task and conceal the possibility of loss. One who stretches out the hand knowingly does not easily let go. The men of the night of ‘Aqabah stretched out exactly that hand.
blocks.75: The fifth place is that of the teacher. To fill a city with faith, one teacher had gone that day, only the Qur’an in his hand. Today in our neighbourhood, with whom do the children learn the Qur’an? How much do we give the maktab teacher, how much do we keep track of?
blocks.76: The sixth place is the tug between home and din. Umm Salamah (RA) wept for a year sitting by the roadside. ‘Ayyash (RA) was turned back in the name of his mother’s oath. Even today our homes have their pull. The call of mother and father, the pressure of relatives, the fear of the home. Not every call is a trap; nor is every call sincere. The word of ‘Umar (RA) was simple; first know who is behind the call.
blocks.77: The seventh place is that of the unnamed people. ‘Ali (RA) lay in the bed. ‘Amir grazed the goats. ‘Abdullah brought news. Asma’ (RA) cut her waistband. ‘Ali (RA) stayed on in Makkah to return the trusts. Today in our mosques, madrasahs, institutions there are such people; they open the door, wash the plates, keep the news. How much do we remember their names?
blocks.78: The eighth place is that of small good. Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) once gave security to the merchants of Quraysh in his area. And the names of those two pulled him up from the roads of Makkah. People with whom today there is only dealing, tomorrow those very ones can come and stand by. No one knows whom and when a small good conduct will serve. There is also Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). In the darkness of the night, informing no one, he used to leave fuel at a widow’s door. Which is our ‘secret’ good deed?
blocks.79: The ninth place is that of the first word. How much of these three is there in our homes today? The salam first to the neighbour. A plate to the hungry house next door. And rising from sleep for at least two rak‘ahs.
blocks.81: In today’s dars we heard the story of searching for a home. Ten years of going from market to market. The six of Yathrib. Then the twelve. The terms of the night of ‘Aqabah; and the hands of the seventy-three. Then the council of Makkah, that bed, the cave on Mount Thawr. Then Suraqah, the white clothes of al-Zubayr (RA), the sun of Quba, the halting of the she-camel.
blocks.82: At the beginning of the dars I put a question. Did the Prophet {{1}} only trust, or did he also calculate? The answer is at the mouth of the cave. The work we leave lying and sit still saying ‘Allah is my trust’, whether the calculation for that work was first made, that is today’s question of the dars. In the next dars we will see what the Prophet {{2}} first built in this new home.
blocks.83: So take one deed with you from today’s dars.
blocks.85: The Prophet {{1}} called for ten years in search of a home, then hid three nights in the cave, and calculated at every step; yet inside the cave he said, Allah is with us.
blocks.86: Today I will ask myself a question: for the work I have left lying saying ‘Allah is my trust’, what calculation have I made? Today I will write a plan for that work on paper, who will do it, what they will do, when they will do it; which I will not leave from today on.

footnotes.0: The announcement of Quraysh’s reward and Suraqah’s pursuit: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum (RA)). The narration is from Suraqah’s own mouth; he was then a polytheist, and believed later. So in the narration of the events no word of honour has been used with his name.
footnotes.1: Sahih al-Bukhari 3652 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), the narration from Abu Bakr’s (RA) mouth)
footnotes.4: The limit of the mursal part: in Sahih al-Bukhari 3906, from ‘Ibn Shihab said: fa-akhbarani ‘Urwatu ibn al-Zubayr anna Rasulallahi {{1}} laqiya al-Zubayra fi rakbin minal Muslimin…’ to the end of the hadith. The part before it (Suraqah’s own narration) has come from a Companion with a connected chain. Support for the main structure of this part of ‘Urwah: Sahih al-Bukhari 3911 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)) and Sahih al-Bukhari 428 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)).
footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; this part is mursal: ‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i, did not name any Companion)
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari 3911 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); the sentence ‘in fact he meant the path of good’ is the narrator’s own explanation
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; this part is mursal: ‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i, did not name any Companion)
footnotes.9: Day and place of arrival: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr; mursal part): ‘wa dhalika yawma al-ithnayni min shahri Rabi‘ al-awwal’. Place: Sahih al-Bukhari 428 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): ‘fa-nazala a‘la al-Madinah fi hayyin yuqalu lahum Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf’. The name ‘Quba’ has come in the narration of al-Hakim 5706 in the portion of Suhayb’s (RA) incident (‘ya‘ni Quba’). Which date of Rabi‘ al-Awwal is not in these narrations; so it is not mentioned here.
footnotes.10: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; this part is mursal: ‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i, did not name any Companion)
footnotes.11: Duration of stay at Quba: Sahih al-Bukhari 428 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): ‘fa-aqama al-Nabiyyu {{1}} fihim arba‘a ‘ashrata laylah’.
footnotes.12: The mosque founded on taqwa: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr; mursal part): ‘wa ussisa al-masjidu alladhi ussisa ‘ala al-taqwa, wa salla fihi Rasulullahi {{1}}’.
footnotes.13: ‘Ali (RA) staying three nights in Makkah and returning the trusts: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on his (peace be upon him) entering Madinah’ (from Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene).
footnotes.14: Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) and the widow of Quba: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on his (peace be upon him) entering Madinah’ (Ibn Ishaq; as the words of ‘Ali (RA)); a narration of the Sirah, as a scene.
footnotes.15: Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 5706 (from Suhayb (RA)); al-Hakim: chain sahih, not narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim; al-Dhahabi: sahih
footnotes.17: The first Jumu‘ah and the calls of the tribes: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on his (peace be upon him) entering Madinah and where his dwelling settled in it’ (from Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene). Ibn Kathir, quoting Ibn Ishaq’s words, said there are various narrations on the duration of stay at Quba (Monday to Thursday; eighteen nights; twenty-two nights; fourteen nights). In this dars the fourteen nights of Sahih al-Bukhari 428 (Anas) have been taken.
footnotes.18: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; this part is mursal: ‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i, did not name any Companion)
footnotes.19: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; this part is mursal: ‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i, did not name any Companion)
footnotes.20: Ownership of the land: in the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (from ‘Urwah; mursal part) the matter of the two orphan boys, and in the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 428 (from Anas (RA)) asking Banu Najjar to fix the price and their saying ‘we ask its price from no one but Allah’. The accounts of the land’s ownership have come in different words in the two narrations; here both have been kept separately with their sources.
footnotes.22: Historical background of beginning the count of years: Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari, explanation of Sahih al-Bukhari 3934. There it is said that the decision to count by Hijri year was taken in the caliphate of ‘Umar (RA). The statement of Sahl ibn Sa‘d (RA) is about this very practice of the Companions.
footnotes.24: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2485 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA)); Imam al-Tirmidhi: sahih
footnotes.25: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2485 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA)); Imam al-Tirmidhi: sahih

quiz.q: After Suraqah fell from the horse, seeing what did the belief arise in his mind that the Prophet’s ﷺ cause will prevail?
o: Seeing the spider’s web, which was at the mouth of the cave; so it seemed
The horse’s legs sinking up to the knees
Seeing a force coming from the sky, mentioned in the verse; therefore
Seeing the Prophet’s ﷺ white garments, which al-Zubayr (RA) had put on him; therefore

quiz.q: You meet suddenly someone who had come to harm you. In the incident of Suraqah, what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: Took him prisoner at once and brought him to the cave
Sent him away with gold, as Suhayb (RA) had given
Gave a written paper of security, and said keep it hidden
Hid him in the cave and made him keep the matter secret

quiz.q: Why is the scene of waiting at the Harrah separately called ‘mursal’?
o: Ibn Hajar called the chain weak, so it is mursal
The narrator was a child at the time of the event, so it is mursal
‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i; he told the event without naming a Companion
The narration is in a book outside Sahih al-Bukhari, so it is mursal
quiz.e: Last part of Sahih al-Bukhari 3906; the main structure matches the narration of Anas (RA) (3911, 428).

quiz.q: Someone asked you who the companion is. What can be learned from Abu Bakr’s (RA) ‘this man guides me on the way’?
o: A lie can be told if the purpose is good, the dars says so
Staying silent at someone’s question is the only way, the dars says so
Always hiding the Prophet’s ﷺ identity is the only means
The word was true, the listener understood it in another sense
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3911 (Anas (RA)); the explanation is the narrator’s.

quiz.q: When Quraysh’s men caught Suhayb (RA) after he had set out, how did he get released?
o: By agreeing to give gold
By asking for a written paper of security like Suraqah
By lying in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed like ‘Ali (RA)
By weaving a spider’s web and covering the mouth of the cave

quiz.q: A man gave up an opportunity of haram income. With whose case in the dars does that match?
o: Suhayb’s (RA); he bought the way with gold
Suraqah’s; following for the greed of a reward, he went back when his horse sank
Abu al-Haytham’s; he asked a question before cutting the old pacts
Abu Ayyub’s (RA), near whose courtyard the she-camel came and halted

quiz.q: Land is needed to build a mosque in your neighbourhood. Which scene would inspire you most?
o: Suraqah falling from his horse when he came to catch, that itself
Abu Bakr (RA) shading the Prophet ﷺ with his cloak, in the sun at Quba, that itself
Asma’ (RA) cutting her waistband and tying the pouch, before the journey to the cave, that itself
Banu Najjar not asking a price and the Prophet ﷺ himself carrying stones

quiz.q: A new neighbour has come. In the light of the Prophet’s ﷺ first word in Madinah, what should be done?
o: Hold a secret meeting with him like at ‘Aqabah
First salam, food and night prayer
Write a paper of security like Suraqah
Call him quickly to faith like the six

quiz.q: A student goes into the exam without opening the book and says ‘Allah is my trust’. According to the dars, what is his statement?
o: Complete tawakkul like the cave of Thawr, where preparation came first
Asking for a promise of security like Suraqah, instead of trust
Not trust; giving his own laziness a beautiful name
Going ahead taking a risk like the night of ‘Aqabah, keeping trust

quiz.q: In the matter of love and honour for the helpers of a new religious project, which hadith does the dars recall?
o: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar
Prayer at its proper time is the most beloved deed
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times more
The first reckoning is of prayer

quiz.q: You have left a task lying, saying ‘Allah is my trust’. What is the first step of the practical resolve?
o: Making a longer du‘a and sitting without calculation, thinking it trust
Asking oneself: what calculation have I made for this task?
Handing the task to someone else and becoming relaxed, thinking it trust
Forgetting the task and drowning in other work, thinking it trust
quiz.e: The ‘Final Word’ and ‘Practical Resolve’ of the dars.
